chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Fudayl ibn Yasar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The one performing an individual Umrah stipulates with his Lord that He releases him wherever he was detained, and the one performing an individual Hajj stipulates with his Lord that if it is not a Hajj, then it is an Umrah.

And there is no harm for the one in Ihram in using what he is obliged to avoid after entering Ihram but before the Talbiyah, such as relations with women, hunting, and perfume, and similar things. So when he says the Talbiyah, all of that becomes forbidden to him, and if he does any of it, the expiation is incumbent upon him. This was narrated.

key_terms.اَلْكَفَّارَةُ: The expiation (kaffarah) for violating Ihram restrictions
key_terms.عُمْرَةً مُفْرَدَةً: Individual Umrah (Umrah performed independently of Hajj)
key_terms.يَشْتَرِطُ عَلَى رَبِّهِ: Stipulates with his Lord (making a conditional vow)

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for prohibited acts during Ihram before and after the Talbiyah?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration to clarify the ritual stipulations (istitraq) for Mufrad pilgrims, distinguishing between the vow for Umrah and the conditional vow for Hajj. It further establishes the precise legal threshold for prohibitions (mahdudat), noting that acts like hunting and using perfume remain permissible before the Talbiyah but become strictly forbidden and subject to expiation (kaffarah) once the Talbiyah is recited.
